accepted.question_text: Given a modulus of continuity ω, construct a compact set K such that the Green function g_{C\K} for the complement C\K with pole at infinity has modulus of continuity comparable to ω. More precisely, require the modulus ω(g_{C\K},·) to be similar to ω, for example by weak equivalence in the sense that there exist constants C1,C2>0 such that C1·ω(δ) ≤ ω(g_{C\K},δ) ≤ C2·ω(δ) for all sufficiently small positive δ.

evidence.quote: Problem 1. Given modulus of continuity ω, find a compact set K such that the modulus of continuity ω(g C\K, ·) is similar to ω.

Here, one can consider similarity as coincidence of moduli on some null sequence or in the sense of weak equivalence: ∃C1, C2 such that C1 ω(δ) ≤ ω(g C\K, δ) ≤ C2 ω(δ) for sufficiently small positive δ.

accepted.question_text: Given a modulus of continuity ω, construct a compact set K for which the Green function g_{C\K} satisfies two-sided pointwise bounds in terms of the distance to K. Specifically, if δ=dist(z,K), require constants C1,C2,δ0>0 independent of z such that C1·ω(δ) ≤ g_{C\K}(z) ≤ C2·ω(δ) whenever δ ≤ δ0.

evidence.quote: A stronger version of the problem is about pointwise estimation of the Green function:
Problem 2. Given modulus of continuity ω, find a compact set K such that C1 ω(δ) ≤ g C\K(z) ≤ C2 ω(δ) for δ = dist(z, K) ≤ δ0, where C1, C1 and δ0 do not depend on z.

accepted.question_text: Find a compact set K contained in the real line for which the Green function g_{C\K} has two-sided Hölder behavior near K. That is, determine whether there exists α>0 and constants C1,C2>0 such that, for all z with sufficiently small δ=dist(z,K), one has C1·δ^α ≤ g_{C\K}(z) ≤ C2·δ^α.
accepted.context_brief: Two-sided Hölder Green function on R

evidence.quote: In the most important case we get a problem about “two-sided H¨older” Green function, which was posed by A. Volberg on his seminar (quoted with permission):
Problem 3. Find a compact set K on the line such that for some α > 0 and constants C1, C2, if δ = dist(z, K) is small enough then C1 δ^α ≤ g C\K(z) ≤ C2 δ^α.

accepted.question_text: Characterize the growth rates of the Markov factors M_n(K), where M_n(K) is the operator norm of differentiation on holomorphic polynomials of degree at most n with the uniform norm on an infinite compact set K, that determine the boundary of the 'zone of uncertainty' for the extension property. Here the extension property means the existence of a continuous linear extension operator from the Whitney function space E(K) to the space of infinitely differentiable functions on R^d.

evidence.quote: Recall that, for a fixed n ∈ N and (infinite) compact set K, the n−th Markov factor Mn(K) is the norm of operator of differentiation in the space of holomorphic polynomials Pn with the uniform norm on K.

By W. Ple´sniak [20], any Markov set K ⊂ R^d has the extension property (EP), which means that there exists a continuous linear extension operator from the space of Whitney functions E(K) to the space of infinitely differentiable functions on R^d.
Problem 4. Characterize the growth rates of Markov’s factors that define the boundaries of the zone of uncertainty for the extension property.

accepted.question_text: Let (f_n) be a regular polynomial sequence, meaning f_n(z)=Σ_{j=0}^{d_n} a_{n,j} z^j with d_n≥2 for every n and with positive constants A1,A2,A3 such that |a_{n,d_n}|≥A1, |a_{n,j}|≤A2|a_{n,d_n}| for 0≤j<d_n, and log|a_{n,d_n}|≤A3 d_n. Assume the generalized Julia set J(f_n) is a Cantor-type subset of the real line. Prove that the recurrence coefficients in the three-term recurrence for the equilibrium measure μ_{J(f_n)} are asymptotically almost periodic, in the sense that they converge to an almost periodic sequence up to an error tending to zero.

evidence.quote: Following [8], we say that (fn) is a regular polynomial sequence (write (fn) ∈ R) if positive constants A1, A2, A3 exist such that for all n ∈ N we have the following three conditions: |an,dn| ≥ A1, |an,j| ≤ A2|an,dn| for j = 0, 1, . . . , dn − 1, log |an,dn| ≤ A3 · dn.

In [6], the authors conjectured that the recurrence coefficients for µK(γ) are asymptotically almost periodic for any γ. It may be hoped that a more general and slightly weaker version of Bellissard’s conjecture can be valid.
Problem 5. Let (fn) be a regular polynomial sequence such that J(fn) is a Cantor-type subset of the real line. Prove that the recurrence coefficients for µJ(fn) are asymptotically almost periodic.

accepted.question_text: Let K be a non-polar compact subset of R, let μ_K be its equilibrium measure, and let P_n(x;μ_K) be the n-th monic orthogonal polynomial with zero set Z_n(μ_K)={x:P_n(x;μ_K)=0}. If U_n(μ_K)=inf{|x-x'|: x,x'∈Z_n(μ_K), x≠x'} denotes the minimal spacing between distinct zeros, determine whether there is a general relationship between this zero spacing and the smoothness of the Green function g_{C\K}; also determine whether there is a general relationship between that zero spacing and the Markov factors of K.
accepted.context_brief: Zero spacing, Green function, Markov factors

evidence.quote: For a measure µ which is supported on R, let Zn(µ) := {x : Pn(x; µ) = 0}. We define Un(µ) by Un(µ) := inf_{x,x′∈Zn(µ), x≠x′} |x − x′|.
In [17], it was shown that Markov’s inequality and spacing of the zeros of orthogonal polynomials are somewhat related.

Problem 6. Let K be a non-polar compact subset of R. Is there a general relation between the zero spacing of orthogonal polynomials for µK and smoothness of gC\K? Is there a relation between the zero spacing of µK and the Markov factors?

accepted.question_text: Let K be a non-polar compact subset of R that is regular with respect to the Dirichlet problem, and let μ be a measure with essential support ess supp(μ)=K whose isolated support points {x_n} satisfy Σ_n g_{C\K}(x_n)<∞. Suppose the logarithmic integrability condition ∫_K log(dμ/dμ_K) dμ_K(x) > -∞ holds, where μ_K is the equilibrium measure on K. Must μ then satisfy either the Widom condition limsup_{n→∞} W_n^2(μ)>0 or the Widom condition 2 liminf_{n→∞} W_n^2(μ)>0? Conversely, if μ satisfies a Widom condition, must the logarithmic integrability condition hold?

Then, as it is discussed in Section 6 of [4], the Szeg˝o condition is equivalent to the condition ∫_K log(dµ/dµK) dµK(x) > −∞. (3)

Problem 7. Let K be a non-polar compact subset of R which is regular with respect to the Dirichlet problem. Let µ be a measure such that ess supp(µ) = K. Assume that the isolated points {xn} of supp(µ) satisfy Σ_n gC\K(xn) < ∞. If the condition (3) is valid for µ is it necessarily true that the Widom condition or the Widom condition 2 holds? Conversely, does the Widom condition imply (3)?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a regular non-polar compact subset K of R that is not a Parreau-Widom set but whose Widom factors W_n(K)=||T_{n,K}||_{L^∞(K)}/Cap(K)^n remain bounded? More specifically, if K has zero Lebesgue measure, must the sequence (W_n(K)) be unbounded? The same questions are asked for the Widom-Hilbert factors (W_n^2(μ_K)) associated with the equilibrium measure μ_K.

evidence.quote: Then we define the n-th Widom factor for K by Wn(K) := ||Tn,K||_{L∞(K)}/Cap(K)^n.
Then the n-th Widom-Hilbert factor for µ is W_n^2(µ) := ||Pn(·; µ)||_{L2(µ)}/(Cap(supp(µ)))^n.

Problem 8. Is it possible to find a regular non-polar compact subset K of R which is not Parreau-Widom but (Wn(K))∞_{n=1} is bounded? If K has zero Lebesgue measure then is it true that (Wn(K))∞_{n=1} is unbounded? We can ask the same problems if we replace (Wn(K))∞_{n=1} by (W_n^2(µK))∞_{n=1} above.

accepted.question_text: Let K be a regular non-polar compact subset of R with leftmost endpoint α, and let μ_K be its equilibrium measure. Assume that μ_K([α,c]) is rational for every c∈R\K. Characterize such sets K. In particular, must every such K be a polynomial generalized Julia set, or equivalently must there exist a sequence (f_n) of admissible polynomials such that, with F_n=f_n∘f_{n-1}∘···∘f_1, the inverse-image sets F_n^{-1}([-1,1]) form a decreasing sequence and K=⋂_{n=1}^∞ F_n^{-1}([-1,1])?
accepted.context_brief: Rational equilibrium masses and generalized Julia sets

evidence.quote: Let TN be a real polynomial of degree N with N ≥ 2 such that it has N real and simple zeros x1 < · · · < xn and N − 1 critical points y1 < · · · < yn−1 with |TN(yi)| ≥ 1 for each i ∈ {1, . . . , N −1}. We call such a polynomial admissible.

Problem 9. Let K be a regular non-polar compact subset of R and α be the leftmost end point of K. Let µK([α, c]) ∈ Q for all c ∈ R \ K. What can we say about K? Is it necessarily a polynomial generalized Julia set? Does this imply that there is a sequence of admissible polynomials (fn)∞_{n=1} such that (F_n^{-1}[-1, 1])∞_{n=1} is a decreasing sequence of sets such that K = ⋂∞_{n=1} F_n^{-1}[-1, 1]?

accepted.question_text: Let K be a non-polar compact subset of R such that the equilibrium measure μ_K coincides with a Hausdorff measure restricted to K. Must the Hausdorff dimension of K be equal to 0?
accepted.context_brief: When equilibrium measure is Hausdorff measure

evidence.quote: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first example of a subset of R such that the equilibrium measure is a Hausdorff measure restricted to the set.
Problem 10. Let K be a non-polar compact subset of R such that µK is equal to a Hausdorff measure restricted to K. Is it necessarily true that the Hausdorff dimension of K is 0?

accepted.question_text: For a regular polynomial sequence (f_n), find simple formulas for the Hausdorff dimension of the measure μ_{J(f_n)} supported on the generalized Julia set J(f_n). Here the Hausdorff dimension of a unit Borel measure μ is defined by dim(μ)=inf{HD(K): μ(K)=1}.
accepted.context_brief: Dimension formulas for Julia-set equilibrium measures

evidence.quote: Hausdorff dimension of a unit Borel measure µ supported on C is defined by dim(µ) := inf{HD(K) : µ(K) = 1} where HD(·) denotes Hausdorff dimension of the given set.
Problem 11. Is it possible to find simple formulas for dim(µJ(fn)) where (fn) is a regular polynomial sequence?
